security_spec.violation_condition: When the Linux kernel context-switches vector state without saving/restoring the full vtype CSR including the new lambda[2:0] (vtype[XLEN-2:XLEN-4]), altfmt_A (vtype[9]), altfmt_B (vtype[10]), and bs (vtype[11]) fields introduced by the Zvvm IME extension, a user process may observe or manipulate another process's IME tile configuration
security_spec.summary: New vtype CSR fields (lambda, altfmt_A, altfmt_B, bs) added by Zvvm IME must be context-switched by the kernel; failure to save/restore these WARL fields leaks IME tile geometry and format state across processes

findings.finding: Correctly saves the full XLEN-wide vtype CSR via csrr, which would capture all Zvvm-defined fields (lambda[2:0], altfmt_A, altfmt_B, bs) on Zvvm hardware. The save side of context-switch is architecturally sound.

Uses vsetvl to restore vtype, but vsetvl architecturally zeroes bits XLEN-2:8 (standard reserved region). On Zvvm hardware, this would silently clobber lambda[2:0] (vtype[XLEN-2:XLEN-4]), altfmt_A (vtype[9]), altfmt_B (vtype[10]), and bs (vtype[11]). The vsetvl instruction is not extensible to preserve non-standard vtype fields, creating a latent architectural gap for any extension that defines those fields.
findings.snippet:
asm volatile (
  ".option push\n\t"
  ".option arch, +zve32x\n\t"
  "vsetvl  x0, %2, %1\n\t"
  ".option pop\n\t"
  "csrw " __stringify(CSR_VSTART) ", %0\n\t"
  : : "r" (src->vstart), "r" (src->vtype), "r" (src->vl));

spec_citations.excerpt: vtype register layout: vill[XLEN-1] | reserved[XLEN-2:8] | vma[7] | vta[6] | vsew[5:3] | vlmul[2:0]. Bits XLEN-2:8 are 'reserved' — vsetvl writes zero to them. Zvvm would redefine bits 9 (altfmt_A), 10 (altfmt_B), 11 (bs), and XLEN-2:XLEN-4 (lambda[2:0]), but vsetvl does not recognize these fields and would zero them.

findings.finding: Calls vsetvli (line 281) and vsetvl (line 291) to reset vector state, which zeroes all vtype bits XLEN-2:8. On Zvvm hardware, this would discard any in-flight IME tile configuration (lambda, altfmt_A, altfmt_B, bs) during explicit vstate discard operations.
findings.snippet:
"vsetvli %0, x0, e8, m8, ta, ma\n\t"
...
"vsetvl  %0, x0, %1\n\t"
: "=&r" (vl) : "r" (vtype_inval));

spec_citations.excerpt: vsetvl/vsetvli write only vlmul[2:0], vsew[2:0], vta, vma, and vill; reserved bits XLEN-2:8 are forced to zero.

findings.finding: Signal frame save correctly delegates to riscv_v_vstate_save() → __vstate_csr_save() which captures full vtype including any Zvvm fields. The vector state (including vtype) is copied to userspace via copy_to_user, preserving all bits.

Signal frame restore sets TIF_RISCV_V_DEFER_RESTORE flag, which causes deferred restore via arch_exit_to_user_mode_prepare() → riscv_v_vstate_restore() → __vstate_csr_restore() → vsetvl. The vsetvl-based restore would zero Zvvm-specific vtype fields on return to userspace after signal delivery.

spec_citations.excerpt: vsetvl zeroes bits XLEN-2:8 where Zvvm fields live.

findings.finding: Deferred vector restore on return to userspace calls riscv_v_vstate_restore() → __riscv_v_vstate_restore() → __vstate_csr_restore() → vsetvl. Zvvm-specific vtype fields would be zeroed on this path, which is the primary context-switch restore surface.

Context-switch path for both preemptive (kernel_vstate) and user (vstate) vector contexts. Save uses __riscv_v_vstate_save (compliant), but restore sets TIF_RISCV_V_DEFER_RESTORE which triggers the vsetvl-based restore on return to userspace. The vsetvl-based restore cannot preserve Zvvm vtype fields.

KVM guest vector restore delegates to __kvm_riscv_vector_restore() → __riscv_v_vstate_restore() → __vstate_csr_restore() → vsetvl. On Zvvm hardware, guest Zvvm vtype fields would be zeroed when the VCPU is loaded, causing guest-visible corruption of IME tile state.

spec_citations.excerpt: vsetvl zeroes bits XLEN-2:8 which would clobber Zvvm-defined vtype fields.

findings.finding: KVM host vector restore uses __kvm_riscv_vector_restore() → vsetvl path. On Zvvm hardware, host Zvvm vtype fields would be zeroed after VM exit, potentially corrupting the host kernel's IME tile configuration.

spec_citations.excerpt: vsetvl zeroes bits XLEN-2:8 where Zvvm lambda/altfmt/bs fields would live.

findings.finding: ptrace vr_set validates vtype against only standard V spec bitmask (VTYPE_VSEW | VTYPE_VLMUL | VTYPE_VMA | VTYPE_VTA). Any bits outside this mask — including Zvvm's lambda, altfmt_A, altfmt_B, bs — are rejected as 'reserved'. A debugger cannot read/write Zvvm vtype fields through ptrace, creating a semantic gap.

spec_citations.excerpt: Standard vtype format shows bits XLEN-2:8 as 'Reserved if non-zero'. ptrace validation enforces this reservation, which would reject valid non-zero Zvvm fields.

findings.finding: Full vector register restore path. Vector registers restored via vle8.v, then CSRs restored via __vstate_csr_restore() → vsetvl. The vsetvl-based vtype restore zeroes vtype bits XLEN-2:8 where Zvvm fields live, even though the in-memory vtype value (restore_from->vtype) correctly retains those bits from the save path.

spec_citations.excerpt: vsetvl writes only vlmul, vsew, vta, vma; XLEN-2:8 (where Zvvm lambda/altfmt/bs live) are set to zero.

findings.finding: In-kernel vector use starts by saving either kernel preempt state or user vstate. Both paths use __riscv_v_vstate_save() → __vstate_csr_save() → csrr, which correctly captures full vtype. Save side is compliant.
When kernel V nesting unwinds to depth 0, restore via __riscv_v_vstate_restore() → __vstate_csr_restore() → vsetvl. Zvvm vtype fields would be zeroed when kernel mode vector operations complete.
